summary: Query Data (BYOB): fetches records from a self-hosted backend class on demand into a records array.
description: The bring-your-own-backend query: when `fetch` fires it runs the configured query against the BYOB backend and emits `records` (array), `count`, `totalCount`, and `firstRecord`. `loading` covers the request window; `success`/`failure` sequence follow-ups. Results are a snapshot — there is no live re-query on remote changes, so writers re-trigger `fetch` when they finish.
whenToUse: Reading lists from a self-hosted backend. On the managed cloud backend prefer Query Records (DbCollection2), which additionally keeps results live.

ports.fetch: Signal; runs the query. Wire a mount signal or a refresh event here.
ports.records: The result array; feeds a Repeater like any items source.
ports.totalCount: Total matching records server-side, independent of paging — drive pagination from this.

runtimeBehavior: Class selection, filter-value inputs and paging inputs are generated from the backend schema and the query configuration (runtime-discovered); only the trigger/result surface is static.
antiPatterns: Expecting live updates after writes — BYOB queries refresh only when `fetch` fires.
